provenance.method: Question assembled from reviewed game descriptions that document short own-pace play, idle/background mode or goal-free construction. The record does not invent save/pause behaviour where sources do not state it.

question: Which games can I inspect if I need to stop or switch away easily?
why_it_matters: Interruptions, fluctuating attention, fatigue or caring responsibilities can make games with long unbreakable sequences or loss on interruption a poor fit.
current_understanding: The Shape of Things is explicitly described as easy to pick up and put down. Gourdlets has an idle-window mode and no objectives or fail states. Townscaper and SUMMERHOUSE are goal-free building experiences, but the current governed sources do not establish their exact autosave or pause behaviour. Treat them as candidates to inspect, not proven interruption-safe choices.
evidence_needed: First-party save, autosave, pause and resume documentation for a wider set of games and platforms.
reopening_conditions: A listed game changes save, pause, session or progression behaviour.
Better platform-specific interruption evidence becomes available.
dissent: A game with no fail state can still be awkward to interrupt if saving, loading or reorientation is difficult; those are separate facets.
